Healing a living subject: Restores 1d6+1 hit points of damage. This cannot grant more hit points than the subject’s normal maximum.

Cancellation: The effects of both potions are cancelled.
This rule does not apply to potions with instantaneous or permanent duration.

response.summary: Move the party one cell, turning to face the way it goes.

Direction.description:
The four grid directions the party faces and moves in.

You use these for the way `MoveParty` steps, the side of a
cell `OpenDoor` works on, and the way a transition turns the
party on arrival. There is no up or down. A
`TransitionSpec` moves the party between levels.

The values are lowercase strings, like `"north"`, and they appear in commands, events, and saves.
Direction.title: Direction

json_schema.description:
Move the party one cell, turning to face the way it goes.

The party must already be in a dungeon. A new session starts in town, and
`EnterDungeon` places the party at the entrance
and switches the session to `exploring`. A step onto a cell the party hasn't explored
uses 10 feet of the party's movement, and a step onto an explored cell uses a third of
that. Each time the movement adds up to the party's exploration rate, one turn passes on
the game clock.

A passage is a `TransitionSpec` whose `kind` is
`"passage"`, standing on one side of a cell. A move toward that side crosses the passage
instead of stopping at the wall there. The party arrives at the passage's destination,
facing its `to_facing`, and the move costs what a step onto that destination cell costs.

Modes:
    `exploring`

Rejections:
    - `session.command.wrong_mode` - the session is not exploring a dungeon.
    - `exploration.move.cannot_move` - the party cannot move: it is overloaded,
      or a living member is unable to walk.
    - `exploration.move.blocked` - a wall, a closed door, an undiscovered secret
      door, or the edge of the map is on that side, and no passage stands there.
    - `exploration.transition.gate_refused` - the move would cross a passage
      whose authored condition (`GateSpec`) the
      party doesn't meet. The rejection includes the gate's authored refusal text.
      Like every refusal, it costs no movement, no time, and no toll.

Events:
    `PartyMovedEvent` with the new position
    and facing. Arriving in the new cell can set off more, each with a
    separate event. A `LocationEnteredEvent`
    follows when the party crosses into a new area, level, or dungeon. A
    `DoorEvent` follows for each unwedged door the party
    opened that swings shut behind it. The area's treasure roll arrives as a
    `HoardGeneratedEvent`. A room
    trap's spring check produces a
    `DetectionRolledEvent` and a
    `TrapEvent`, and a trap that springs
    resolves at once.

    A pool of burning oil or a *web* on the cell affects the party as it arrives
    (`DamageDealtEvent`,
    `HitPointsReportedEvent`,
    `DeathEvent`,
    `EffectAttachedEvent`,
    `ConditionGainedEvent`). Monsters keyed to
    the area in the adventure (a keyed encounter) meet the party the first time it enters,
    with `SurpriseRolledEvent`s,
    `EncounterStartedEvent`,
    `ReactionRolledEvent`, and
    `StanceChangedEvent`. When their reaction is
    to attack, battle opens at once
    (`BattleStartedEvent`).

    A move through a passage reports the crossing before the step, as
    `UseStairs` does. An
    `ItemConsumedEvent` comes first when
    the passage's gate takes an item as a toll. A `LocationEnteredEvent` follows when the
    level or dungeon changes, with `via` set to `"passage"` and `transition_ref`
    set to the passage's cell. Then come the `DoorEvent`s for the doors that swing shut
    on the level the party left, the `PartyMovedEvent` for the landing cell, and the
    landing cell's events.

    When the step's movement completes a turn on the game clock, the events of that turn
    follow:
    `EffectExpiredEvent` with a
    `LightEvent` for a light burning out,
    `FatigueEvent` when the fatigue penalty starts or ends,
    `ProvisionsEvent` on a day boundary,
    and `WanderingCheckEvent` when a
    wandering-monster check is due.

command_type.description:
The name that identifies the command class in serialized data. Each command class fixes
it to a distinct snake_case string, like `"move_party"` or `"open_door"`, and constructing
the class sets it, so you never pass it yourself.
`parse_command` and the
`AnyCommand` union use it to rebuild the right class
from a serialized mapping. A class's value never changes between releases.
command_type.title: Command Type

source.description:
Who or what issued the command on whose behalf: an authored trigger or quest id, or the
name of one of your game's systems. The engine never reads it, so a command with a
`source` does exactly what the same command without one does. The session logs and
replays it with the command, so the log alone shows why something happened. Leave it
`None` when there's nothing to record. An empty string fails validation when the command
is constructed.
source.title: Source

direction.description:
Which way to step. The party turns to face that way as it goes, so a move is also a turn.
To change facing without moving, use `TurnParty`. A
direction with a wall, a closed door, an undiscovered secret door, or the edge of the map
on that side of the party's cell gets the refusal `exploration.move.blocked`, unless a
passage stands on that side. Read
`ExploredLevelView.edges` to find which sides
of the cell the party can leave by.

json_schema.title: MoveParty

adventure.name: The Barrow of the Forgotten King
adventure.description: A plundered barrow outside town, and the idol the temple wants back.
hooks: The temple pays 200 gp for the Jade Idol's return.

town.name: Threshold
town.description: A walled market town at the edge of the moors.

areas.name: Guard room
areas.description: Broken spears and gnawed bones litter the flagstones.

areas.name: Shrine of the Barrow King
areas.description: A toppled altar; something green glints beneath it.

features.description: The idol rests in a hollow under the altar stone.

levels.guidance: Grave goods, not treasure: the barrow king was buried, not hoarded. Keep the goblins squalid and the shrine quiet.

areas.name: Looted vault
areas.description: Empty niches, but one flagstone sits proud of the floor.

levels.guidance: Somebody else is always down here first. Rivals are rude, not evil.

items.name: Jade Idol of the Barrow King

narrative.progress: The idol comes up out of the hollow, cold as well-water.
Threshold's gate shuts behind you with the idol inside it.

narrative.offer: The temple wants the Jade Idol off the barrow king's altar and back on its own.
narrative.completion: The almoner counts out the reward without looking up. The idol is home.
narrative.speaker: the temple almoner

journal.text: The temple wants the Jade Idol off the barrow king's altar and back on its own.
